observations.body: PROGRAMMING Artist Lineup Tonight’s sets, resident bands, and curated genres. Performance Archive Legendary nights, captured in smoke, brass, and velvet. Experiences Fine dining, private lounge, and bottle service rituals. Reserve JAZZ LOUNGE & SUPPER CLUB • DOWNTOWN Sonic Gastronomy for nights that linger. The Midnight Note is a charcoal-dark listening room where brass glows, plates arrive on cue, and every set is paced like a tasting menu. Reserve a table for tonight’s program—or apply for membership to unlock late-night access and cellar selections. Reserve Seats Explore Tonight’s Lineup Doors 6:30 • First set 7:30 Chef’s Tasting (5 courses) • Limited Dress: evening casual Tonight • “Blue Hour” Trio • 9:45 set A slow-rotating brass ring echoes cymbal shimmer—our signature motif for sound in motion. Sensory Pillars Three entrances to the same night: the music, the menu, and the room itself. Tap a pillar to expand the experience. Listen Curated sets with vinyl warmth and stage intimacy. Taste Seasonal courses timed to the set list. Feel Listening Room Protocol Our stage is mixed for clarity, not volume. Sets are framed by short intermissions—enough time to refresh a drink, not enough to break the spell. House system tuned for upright bass definition and cymbal air. Vinyl prelude from the club library before each first set. Quiet service choreography; menus land between tunes. Chef’s Set Menu: “Midnight Service” Five courses built around late-night brightness—citrus, smoke, and slow heat—paired to the pacing of the evening’s program. First course arrives with the opening theme—clean, bracing, precise. Main course lands before the final solo—comforting and deep. Dessert is plated during applause—quiet sweetness, no rush. Room Atmosphere Low tables, deep banquettes, and a ceiling designed to scatter reflections like brushwork—soft edges, clean detail. The room is calibrated for closeness: you’ll feel the cymbal swell before you notice it. Candlelight speculars across glass and brass. Sapphire-blue gradients in the lounge, velvet violet at the bar. Seat spacing optimized for conversation between sets. M Artist Lineup Four pillars of sound, each with its own cadence. Filter by vibe to shape your night. Fine Dining Chef’s set menu, timed to the music Tonight’s Tasting Sequence A five-course progression designed for a listening room: clean flavors early, smoky depth at the midpoint, and a final sweet note that doesn’t compete with the stage. First Chorus Citrus + sea salt, chilled and bright $24 Second Chorus Charred seasonal vegetables, herb oil $28 Headliner Slow-roasted entrée, warm spice finish $52 Encore Bittersweet dessert, espresso crema $18 Service is paced around the set list Private Lounge Booth seating, bottle service, and late sets Booth Rituals & Bottle Program The lounge runs on sapphire light and quiet confidence. Bottle service is curated for texture: mineral whites, velvet reds, and a short list of late-night pours. Cellar Select (Red) Decanted on request • dark fruit & spice $145 Mineral White Chilled • crisp finish for first set $118 Midnight Spark Fine bubbles • for celebrations and encores $165 Spirits Flight Three pours • paired to the band’s tempo $62 Sapphire booths • late-night pours Questions, answered quietly A few details—so your night moves without friction. Is it a listening room? Yes. Conversation is welcomed between sets; during performances we keep service quiet and ask guests to keep voices low. Think: supper club energy with concert-level attention. How long is a typical visit? Plan for two sets plus intermission—about 2 hours. Chef’s tasting runs with the first set and finishes during the encore. Lounge bookings are typically 2.5 hours. Do you offer non-alcoholic pairings? We do. The “Brass & Citrus” pairing focuses on botanicals, tea infusions, and carbonation—built to complement the menu without overwhelming the room. Guest Reviews Praise that reads like a set list: tight, warm, and specific. Scroll for more. Clara M. Reserved for the 7:30 set • Chef’s tasting 5/5 ♪ “The room is tuned like an instrument. You can hear the brushwork, and the service never interrupts it. Courses arrived exactly between tunes—felt composed.” MN Midnight Notes JL Jazz Ledger Amira S. Late set • Date night 5/5 ♪ “It’s the softest kind of drama: neon accents, velvet corners, and a band that plays like they’re telling secrets. The room breathes.” SR Supper Review NW Night Wire Club Records Numbers that tell a story—sets played, cocktails built, and the artists who have crossed our stage. +500 Shows performed since opening night +80 Signature cocktails in the Midnight Book +12 Grammy winners hosted for special sets Performance Archive Browse nights that shaped the room. Hover or tap an entry to reveal a photographic memory with subtle parallax. The residency defined our sound: a bass you can trace with your eyes, a ride cymbal that blooms instead of bites. mobile_observations.body: PROGRAMMING Artist Lineup Tonight’s sets, resident bands, and curated genres. Performance Archive Legendary nights, captured in smoke, brass, and velvet. Experiences Fine dining, private lounge, and bottle service rituals. Reserve JAZZ LOUNGE & SUPPER CLUB • DOWNTOWN Sonic Gastronomy for nights that linger. The Midnight Note is a charcoal-dark listening room where brass glows, plates arrive on cue, and every set is paced like a tasting menu. Reserve a table for tonight’s program—or apply for membership to unlock late-night access and cellar selections. Reserve Seats Explore Tonight’s Lineup Doors 6:30 • First set 7:30 Chef’s Tasting (5 courses) • Limited Dress: evening casual Tonight • “Blue Hour” Trio • 9:45 set A slow-rotating brass ring echoes cymbal shimmer—our signature motif for sound in motion. Sensory Pillars Three entrances to the same night: the music, the menu, and the room itself. Tap a pillar to expand the experience. Listen Curated sets with vinyl warmth and stage intimacy. Taste Seasonal courses timed to the set list. Feel Listening Room Protocol Our stage is mixed for clarity, not volume. Sets are framed by short intermissions—enough time to refresh a drink, not enough to break the spell. House system tuned for upright bass definition and cymbal air. Vinyl prelude from the club library before each first set. Quiet service choreography; menus land between tunes. Chef’s Set Menu: “Midnight Service” Five courses built around late-night brightness—citrus, smoke, and slow heat—paired to the pacing of the evening’s program. First course arrives with the opening theme—clean, bracing, precise. Main course lands before the final solo—comforting and deep. Dessert is plated during applause—quiet sweetness, no rush. Room Atmosphere Low tables, deep banquettes, and a ceiling designed to scatter reflections like brushwork—soft edges, clean detail. The room is calibrated for closeness: you’ll feel the cymbal swell before you notice it. Candlelight speculars across glass and brass. Sapphire-blue gradients in the lounge, velvet violet at the bar. Seat spacing optimized for conversation between sets. M Artist Lineup Four pillars of sound, each with its own cadence. Filter by vibe to shape your night. Fine Dining Chef’s set menu, timed to the music Tonight’s Tasting Sequence A five-course progression designed for a listening room: clean flavors early, smoky depth at the midpoint, and a final sweet note that doesn’t compete with the stage. First Chorus Citrus + sea salt, chilled and bright $24 Second Chorus Charred seasonal vegetables, herb oil $28 Headliner Slow-roasted entrée, warm spice finish $52 Encore Bittersweet dessert, espresso crema $18 Service is paced around the set list Private Lounge Booth seating, bottle service, and late sets Booth Rituals & Bottle Program The lounge runs on sapphire light and quiet confidence. Bottle service is curated for texture: mineral whites, velvet reds, and a short list of late-night pours. Cellar Select (Red) Decanted on request • dark fruit & spice $145 Mineral White Chilled • crisp finish for first set $118 Midnight Spark Fine bubbles • for celebrations and encores $165 Spirits Flight Three pours • paired to the band’s tempo $62 Sapphire booths • late-night pours Questions, answered quietly A few details—so your night moves without friction. Is it a listening room? Yes. Conversation is welcomed between sets; during performances we keep service quiet and ask guests to keep voices low. Think: supper club energy with concert-level attention. How long is a typical visit? Plan for two sets plus intermission—about 2 hours. Chef’s tasting runs with the first set and finishes during the encore. Lounge bookings are typically 2.5 hours. Do you offer non-alcoholic pairings? We do. The “Brass & Citrus” pairing focuses on botanicals, tea infusions, and carbonation—built to complement the menu without overwhelming the room. Noah K. • Programming Kitchen 5 min read Why our tasting menu lands between tunes Timing is a flavor. We design each course so the last bite resolves before the next downbeat.
